title: We now know how radiation destroys electronics devices | New Scientist
description: A detailed picture of how a single particle of radiation can destroy a semiconductor device could offer pointers for how to make electronics more resilient to the harsh conditions of space
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI's environmental footprint | New Scientist
description: Turkey, which is co-hosting the COP31 climate summit, hoped countries would back efforts to rein in the carbon emissions of the AI build-out, but few were prepared to endorse the pledge
author: Manuela Callari

title: Plans to rely on carbon removal tech spark debate at COP31 | New Scientist
description: Some countries at the COP31 summit are calling to accelerate the deployment of carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture, but critics argue these approaches are unproven at scale and distract from efforts to phase out fossil fuels
author: Manuela Callari

title: Nuclear bomb in space would disable 98 per cent of satellites within a week | New Scientist
description: Just one nuclear explosion in space would have global and long-lasting repercussions, disabling almost every satellite and creating technological chaos from which it would take years to recover, warn experts
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Massive data centres collectively use as much electricity as an entire US state | New Scientist
description: The largest data centres in the US are responsible for about 2 per cent of the country's entire annual electricity use
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Skeleton found in Denmark came from man who witnessed the arrival of farming | New Scientist
description: Clues about the diet of “Rødhals Man”, who lived some 6000 years ago, hint that he lived through one of the most revolutionary changes in human history
author: Chris Simms
